title: RERA Advertisement Rules: What Every Real Estate Ad Must Show (2026)
seoTitle: RERA Advertisement Rules 2026: Checklist for Property Ads
excerpt: RERA advertisement rules: no ads before registration, RERA number and website in every ad, UP RERA and MahaRERA QR codes, CP duties and penalties.

faqs.question: What are the RERA rules for real estate advertisements?
faqs.answer: A project that must be registered cannot be advertised before registration (Section 3 of the RERA Act, 2016). After registration, every advertisement must prominently show the registration number and the state authority's website address (Section 11(2)). States add their own directions, such as UP RERA's project QR code.

faqs.question: Is the RERA number mandatory in social media ads?
faqs.answer: Yes. RERA's definition of advertisement covers publicity in any medium, so Facebook, Instagram, Google and YouTube ads, WhatsApp broadcasts and posts by channel partners all need the project's registration number and the authority's website address, shown where people can read it, plus the QR code in states that require one.

faqs.question: Is a QR code mandatory in UP RERA advertisements?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since July 2024 UP RERA assigns each project a unique QR code and requires promoters to print it in brochures and advertisements and on documents given to buyers, such as booking forms, allotment letters and builder-buyer agreements. In January 2025 it reminded promoters this covers print, outdoor, TV, digital and social media.

faqs.question: Is a QR code mandatory in MahaRERA advertisements?
faqs.answer: Yes. MahaRERA has required a project QR code in advertisements since August 2023, and its April 2025 directions require a scannable QR code at the top right of every ad, with registration details in a large enough font. They apply to promoters and agents, with penalties of up to ₹50,000.

faqs.question: Can a builder advertise a project before RERA registration?
faqs.answer: No. Section 3(1) bars a promoter from advertising, marketing, booking, selling or inviting people to buy units in a project that must be registered until it is registered. The penalty is up to 10% of the estimated project cost under Section 59.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for an advertisement without the RERA number?
faqs.answer: For a promoter, breaking Section 11(2) can attract a penalty of up to 5% of the estimated project cost under Section 61. For an agent who breaks the agent rules, the penalty is up to ₹10,000 a day, up to 5% of the cost of the unit, under Section 62.

faqs.question: What happens if a real estate ad makes a false claim?
faqs.answer: Under Section 12, if a buyer pays based on false or incorrect information in an advertisement, prospectus or model apartment and suffers a loss, the promoter must compensate them. If the buyer withdraws, the promoter must refund the money with interest and compensation.

faqs.question: Do channel partners have to follow RERA advertising rules?
faqs.answer: Yes. Agents must be RERA-registered (Section 9), must not market unregistered projects and must not use unfair trade practices such as false statements (Section 10). Their ads are ads for the project, so they need the project's registration number and authority website, and usually the agent's own number.

faqs.question: Does RERA apply to commercial property ads?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Act's definition of apartment includes offices, shops, showrooms and godowns, so commercial projects above the size limits must register and follow the same advertising rules as residential ones: no ads before registration, and the registration number and authority website in every ad.
